children: Wells Fargo Investment Institute’s “misery index” is sustainably high.

This index combines nominal gas prices with the inverse of a housing affordability index, or the ratio of the median family income to the income needed to qualify for the median-priced home, according to Wells Fargo.

“Historically, the index has had an inverse relationship with consumer spending growth, particularly during periods of sharp movement. However, the relationship has weakened in recent years, highlighting the resilience of consumer spending despite mounting pressure on household budgets,” analysts said.

Recent strength in household demand was due to the recent stock market rise, moderate employment growth, and periods of declining inflation that boosted income, Wells Fargo added. These economic tailwinds loosened the link between spending and "misery" even amid household affordability pressures.

“We believe resilient consumers will support broader economic growth, even as elevated interest rates weigh on housing affordability and the economy’s other credit-sensitive areas,” analysts concluded.

title: Household misery remains elevated despite strong consumers, says Wells Fargo
